title: Commands
body: `docc init` creates `docc.json`, `docs/schemas/page.json` and `docs/src/index.json` (kind page) if they do not exist and builds `docs/out`, so the first check is green. The configuration it writes has `maxWarnings` 0, so a warning such as a stale link (DOC209) fails `docc check`, and it adds the single-file builds (`docs/out.md`, `docs/out.html`, `docs/out-full*`) to `.gitignore`. In a git repository without a pre-commit hook it also writes `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, which runs `docc check`, so a commit with invalid documentation is refused; an existing hook is never touched.
`docc validate` checks the sources and prints the diagnostics. It changes no files.

`docc build` writes the Markdown into `docs/out`, removes the files it generated earlier that no source produces any more (pages with the GENERATED mark, copies of images, file manager junk) and updates `docc.lock`. When the folder holds any other file it refuses with exit code 2, writes and deletes nothing and lists those files: links that are not in the lock are recorded as confirmed, links that are gone are dropped. When the sources have errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx it writes nothing and exits with code 1. With the flag full it writes the audit build into `docs/out-full` and leaves `docs/out` alone.

The flags single and html add one file next to the folder, each can be combined with full: `docc build --single` writes all pages into one Markdown file (`docs/out.md`) and `docc build --html` into one self-contained HTML application (`docs/out.html`) to read and comment on: a timeline of the saved versions with the edits drawn in the text, and comments ([[rendering]]). The folder of pages is built as before. Once made, such a file is rebuilt by every later `docc build`, with or without the flag, so a stale file is never sent, if docc wrote it; a file of another origin is left alone with a message on stderr, and only the flag replaces it. `--since <revision>` names the version a reader last saw (a tag, branch or commit): the HTML file shows the edits since it and keeps no history before it; a bad revision stops only the HTML file: the diagnostics are still printed and the exit code is 2. `--page <path>` writes one page alone: its path relative to the source folder as `docc compile` gives it (with or without `.json`) or its id; the output folder gets only that page and the pictures it shows (no other page, no `_tree.md`, until a build without the flag), and the one-file builds hold only that page; an unknown page, or a hidden one without full, is an error with exit code 2. `--rev <revision>` builds the tree of a Git revision without a checkout, as `docc compile --rev` reads it (a bare mirror with `--config` too): it needs `--html`, refuses `--single` and writes only the HTML file, into the current folder, with the history up to that revision; the output folder and `docc.lock` are not written. The readers' comments stand under their blocks in the pages and the HTML file, and `--no-comments` leaves them out of everything the build writes. These files are for reading, are not committed and are not checked by `docc check`. With full they are `docs/out-full.md` and `docs/out-full.html`.

`docc compile --format json` is for a program that shows the pages itself, such as Docspace. It prints one JSON object on one line and writes nothing: no `docs/out`, no `docc.lock`. The object holds `$schema` (the version of its shape), `ok`, the `summary` and the full list of `diagnostics` as validate reports them, the `project` (title, lang, branding), the `tree` and the `pages` a reader sees, without hidden documents and notes. A page has its id, its path below src, title, kind, status, tags, parent, breadcrumbs, the one-line fields of the property list, its `sections` (the headings of fields and `$sections`, with the anchor that links use as id) its `blocks`: JSON Pointer, source text, HTML (the same as in the HTML file) and the section the block stands under, and its `comments`: the readers' comments of `$comments` without their email, each with its place (same, changed or lost). The object is printed in every case: with errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx the tree and the pages are empty, and a failure (a bad `docc.json`, an unknown revision) is one diagnostic of code `config`, `usage` or `error` with exit code 2. The exit code is that of validate. `--rev` compiles the tree of a Git revision (a commit, branch or tag) without a checkout: every file of the project comes from that revision, read with `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file --batch`, so includes and links resolve in it and the positions of the diagnostics are those of its files. In a bare repository `--config docs/docc.json` names the project folder. `docc schema compile` prints the JSON Schema of the object.

`docc log --format json` and `docc diff <base> <head> --format json` give the same program the history, read from Git without a checkout (a bare mirror with `--config` too). `docc log` lists the commits of the first-parent chain of `--rev` (default HEAD) that changed anything in the source folder, newest first, down to `--since` (not included; a commit off that chain is an error): full hashes, parents, author, committer, date, subject and body, and each changed file with its status (A, M, D, R with the old path), id, title and how many blocks it added, changed and removed. A deleted document keeps its last title, a file that is not valid JSON is marked broken and counted against its last good version, a document hidden in that version is marked hidden (with its counts; the version that shows it counts all its blocks as added, as the diff does), and a change only inside the top-level `$comments` is comments-only (a commit is when all its files are). `docc diff` compiles each side from its own revision, as `docc compile --rev` does, and lines up the blocks of every changed document: an operation same, add, rm or ch with the block on each side in the shape of compile; without `--path` only the changes, with `--path` one document with every block in an order for two columns. The base may be the empty tree, for a root commit. Both use the one alignment of blocks the HTML history uses, so the counts of the log are the operations of the diff. `docc schema log` and `docc schema diff` print their JSON Schemas.

`docc check` is read-only and made for CI. It runs validate, then compares `docs/out` with what the sources produce, with or without the comments (DOC501; not with `"commitOut": false`), and `docc.lock` with the links in the sources (DOC503). With errors of the groups 1xx or 2xx the comparison is skipped.

`docc ack` takes document ids, link targets or code files and sets the stored hashes in `docc.lock` to the current ones for every changed line whose source or target is the argument, or whose target lies in the document with that id. Lines that did not change are left alone. It prints each link it confirmed (`confirmed source -> target`; in JSON a `links` list) and the total, so the reader sees which sources were confirmed. It is run after a person has checked every source flagged by DOC209 or DOC402. `docc ack --all` confirms every changed link.

`docc update` replaces the running binary with a release from GitHub. It reads `checksums.txt` of the release, picks the archive for this system, refuses it when the SHA-256 differs and only then swaps the file. The flag check only reports whether a newer release exists (exit code 1: there is one), the flag version takes a given tag. A development build without a release version refuses to update. The variable DOCC_BASE_URL replaces the releases address, `install.sh` and `install.ps1` read it too.

`docc comments` handles the readers' comments, which live in the documents themselves, in the top-level member `$comments` ([[document-model#comments]]). Without a subcommand (or with list) it prints every comment with its document, the text of its block now and its place: same, changed (the block was edited) or lost (no block at its pointer, its words are gone, or the answered form field is not there). `docc comments apply` reads a JSON array of operations from standard input, add (a document id or path and the comment; a missing id and creation time are filled in), rm (an id) and edit (an id and the text that replaces the old one, or for an answer to a form field the answer that replaces it: the comment stays an answer to the same field, follows the field if it moved, quotes it as it reads now and keeps its creation time; every edit keeps `created` and sets `edited` to the time now, in UTC like `created`, a second edit overwrites it, and add never sets it), and edits the files in place: only `$comments` changes and every other byte of a file stays; a `$comments` that was not there is added as the last member of the document, indented like the file, and it goes away with its last comment. A comment stands only where a reader looks, one rule for the CLI, the import and Docspace: `at` must be the pointer of a block, a property or (for an answer) the form field that `docc compile` shows on the page of that document, so notes, `docIgnore`, `hidden`, the title and `$comments` itself are refused; `quote` is always the source text of that block, and a quote given is replaced. A hidden document takes no comment, and rm and edit leave its comments alone, unless `--hidden` is given (an agent working by hand; Docspace never gives it). rm and edit refuse an id that more than one comment of the project has (DOC112). While the project has errors of groups 1xx-2xx readers see no page, so add is refused. One bad operation fails the batch with exit code 2 and nothing is written; with `--format json` it prints what it added (with the ids it made), removed and edited and the files it wrote, in the shape `docc schema comments-apply` prints. `docc comments import <file>` (`-` reads the copied text from standard input) writes the comments of the HTML file, copied as text or downloaded, into their documents through apply: a comment already there (same id) is skipped, a comment left on an older build follows its block to where it stands now, an answer goes to its form field, and a comment that would not stand where a reader looks (a hidden document or part, a block that is gone) is skipped and listed, like one on a page that is gone. `docc comments rm <id>` deletes comments through apply; an id may be shortened to a unique prefix. There are no statuses and no replies: a comment that was handled is deleted in the same commit as the fix.
Every command accepts --help and prints its flags with an example. The global flags may stand before or after the command. `docc init` ends with a Next block of steps.

`docc explain` takes a code in any case (doc209), a name (style/hedging) or a group (graph, style): a rule with an example, or for a group the list of its rules. `docc rules` lists the rules with their effective levels; `docc schema document`, `docc schema config`, `docc schema compile`, `docc schema log` and `docc schema diff` print the JSON Schemas.
The settings are in [[config]] and the generated pages in [[rendering]].
flags: format text or json, config, max-diagnostics (default 20, errors first, applies to both formats, 0 means no limit, negative values are rejected), max-warnings.
exit_codes: 1: errors, or more effective warnings than the limit.

2: wrong usage or configuration, including a missing source folder or a kind schema that does not load. The message goes to stderr; with `--format json` it is the usual report (`summary`, `diagnostics`) with diagnostics of code `config`, `usage` or `error`, and every error of `docc.json` is listed at once.
